problem: Existing trainable LLM-based VLN agents (e.g. NaviLLM) map inputs directly to actions with no explicit reasoning, so decisions are uninterpretable and learning is harder. Fixed-label CoT SFT is also hard because perfect navigation CoT labels do not exist, and it overfits to the label distribution.
motivation: CoT training can improve both accuracy and interpretability for embodied agents. But navigation has multiple valid cues per step, so a single fixed CoT label is noisy and narrow. Free-form GPT-generated CoT is slow and redundant for sequential decision making.
key_idea: Train an LLM navigation agent with concise formalized landmark+direction CoT labels, then post-train it on its own correct reasoning outputs as self-enriched CoT labels plus a self-reflective positive-vs-negative reasoning discrimination task.
insight: Stage 1 formalized CoT SFT alone lifts R2R val-unseen IL SPL from 43.78 to 46.26. Self-enriched labels (47.98) and the self-reflective task (47.86) each help, and combining them gives the best SR/SPL (51.15/48.27). This suggests that diversifying supervision with the model's own decision-verified reasoning reduces overfitting. Formalized labels beat free-form CoT (SPL 62.05 vs 60.95) and are about 3x faster (2.5s vs 7.8s per step), and both landmark and direction are needed.
method: Model architecture: NaviLLM-style agent (scene encoder + LLM + action head) whose prompt ends with '-Action Decision: <cls>. -Navigational Reasoning:'. It generates CoT text and the <cls> feature drives action prediction.

Formalized CoT label collection: for the GT observation, Tag2Text captions the image, Spacy extracts landmarks, and heading/elevation is mapped to a direction word. These fill the template 'I should go to an observation with [L] to the [D] of me'.
Stage 1 formalized CoT SFT: L = L_action + λ·L_SFT (autoregressive CoT loss, λ=1). L_SFT is applied with probability 0.5 to reduce overfitting; full-parameter fine-tuning trained to convergence.

Self-enriched CoT label enhancement (Stage 2): if the model's predicted action equals the GT action, its own reasoning R_t replaces the template label as the CoT target; otherwise the original label is kept.

Self-reflective auxiliary task: the prompt shows two reasoning outputs, the positive (CoT label) and a negative built from a random non-GT candidate's landmark/direction in random order, and the model answers 'Output 1/2'. Loss L_sr, weight 0.2.
Stage 2 objective: L = L_action + λ1·L_SFT + λ2·L_sr with LoRA. Stage 1 is trained to convergence first to avoid noisy or degenerate self-labels.

setting.backbone: NaviLLM (LLM backbone, Vicuna-based) with scene encoder and action head, fine-tuned (full-parameter in Stage 1, LoRA in Stage 2)
setting.training_data: Benchmark training sets (R2R, CVDN, REVERIE, SOON) with auto-generated formalized CoT labels from Tag2Text+Spacy; no NaviLLM pretraining phase; task-specific or cross-task multi-dataset training; no extra environments
setting.observation: Panoramic RGB views (navigable candidate views) plus navigation history features and instruction
setting.action_space: Discrete nav-graph navigable viewpoints plus stop
setting.privileged: none at test time (GT actions/observations are used only to build training labels)

results: EvolveNav beats the reimplemented NaviLLM baseline on all four benchmarks. R2R val-unseen SPL rises from 60.25 to 63.48, and CVDN GP from 5.53 to 6.21. In IL, R2R SPL rises from 43.78 to 48.27. It still trails cross-modal specialists such as DUET and AZHP on REVERIE and SOON.
limitations: Gains are measured against a reimplemented NaviLLM without its pretraining, and still lag cross-modal SOTA on REVERIE/SOON.
CoT labels depend on the noisy Tag2Text captions and Spacy extraction, and self-labels are chosen only by action correctness.
Two-stage training is costly (Stage 1 needs 8 A100s for ~1.5 days) and only simulator R2R-style benchmarks are evaluated, with no real robot.
